extracted.intended_audience: general public, people interested in misinformation and journalism (including journalists and media consumers)
extracted.subtask_description: A TED Talk landing page describing Olga Yurkova's presentation about StopFake.org and strategies to combat Russian disinformation and reduce the spread of fake news. The page summarizes the talk's purpose and promises two concrete ways to avoid reading or sharing fake news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "When facts are false, decisions are wrong."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the core principle that false facts lead to poor decisions; presented as the motivating justification for anti-misinformation work. No specific evaluative tests provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose biased or inaccurate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: StopFake.org "exposes biased or inaccurate reporting in order to rebuild the trust we've lost in our journalists, leaders and institutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies a journalistic quality criterion: identify and publicize bias/inaccuracy to restore public trust. The page cites StopFake.org's mission but provides no operational checklist or methods here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reading or sharing fake news (two critical ways)
rubrics_metrics.description: The talk promises "two critical ways we can ensure we're not reading (or sharing) fake news."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates there are actionable consumer-focused steps to verify information and curb sharing of misinformation; the specific two ways are not listed on this summary page.
